title: Q4 cadence orchestration & exec snapshot (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc drafts a compact, cross-functional cadence for the upcoming Q4 planning window and provides an "exec snapshot" for leadership updates and the all-hands. Target audience: execs + leads who will review OKR framing, commitments, and immediate risks before the Q4 kickoff.

High-level ask (single sentence):
Agree to the company-level OKR framing and commit to the 6-week cadence trial for cross-functional initiatives, with a decision checkpoint at Week 7.

Context and constraints:
- Company priorities: stabilize Hosted API latency at P95 <= 180ms for common prompt shapes, complete Redwood Dedicated public beta steps, and open the private deployment onboarding pipeline for two pilot customers.
- Resourcing: hiring freeze for non-critical IC roles until budget review (Finance brief in Week 2). Leaders may need to re-prioritize feature-scope into Q1 if hires are delayed.
- Customer signals: 3 large prospects asked for Dedicated SLAs and on-prem evaluation timelines in the last 30 days (see linked Jira EPIC INF-1123).

Proposed company-level OKRs (draft for discussion)
OKR 1 (Reliability & Latency): Reduce production-hosted tail latency and error surface for steady-state workloads.
- KR1.1: P95 latency for typical gen endpoint <= 180ms across top-10 routes (measured avg across two regions)
- KR1.2: Error rate (5xx) for gen endpoints <= 0.03% over rolling 30d
- KR1.3: Deploy streaming fallback flow to 3 major customers (internal rollout + docs)

OKR 2 (Commercial & Capacity): Convert demand into predictable commitments while preserving unit economics.
- KR2.1: Close 3 Dedicated reserved deals with minimum 1 GPU-month commit each
- KR2.2: Reduce avg cost-per-1M tokens for Hosted API by 12% (ops + model selection + caching)
- KR2.3: Complete private onboarding playbook and run 2 pilot deployments end-to-end

OKR 3 (Developer Experience & Observability): Reduce iteration friction for platform users and internal teams.
- KR3.1: Release v1 of the Console tracing UI with per-route token-cost breakdowns
- KR3.2: Ship SDK v2 with improved error semantics and 2 new language bindings
- KR3.3: Create 40 prompt/eval checks and tie regression alerts to CI for top-5 customer flows

Notes on metrics and stretch targets:
- KR thresholds intentionally conservative for reliability-focused OKR 1. If funding allows, recommend stretch P95 target of 150ms.
- Cost target (KR2.2) assumes shipping both a KV-cache promotion and small-quantization pilot for text gen workloads.

Proposed cadence: 6-week company sprint (trial)
Why 6 weeks?
- Balances end-to-end deliverables for cross-functional initiatives (eng, product, SRE, sales) while allowing short-term tactical adjustments.
- Better for customer pilots (onboarding + feedback loop) than 2-week sprint format for company-level features.
Cadence structure:
- Week 0 (pre-kick): OKR finalization, stakeholder sign-offs, release calendar aligned
- Weeks 1–5: Focused execution (weekly syncs, initiative triage hour)
- Week 6: Demo week + exec checkpoint + retrospective + roll decision into next cycle

Cross-functional rituals (must-haves)
- Weekly cross-functional sync (30 min): ops + product + eng leads — short surfacing of blockers, capacity conflicts, and risk flags.
- Initiative triage hour (optional): engineers/product owners meet mid-week to rebalance cross-team work.
- Demo day (end of Week 6): 45–60 minute recorded show-and-tell for execs + select customers.

All-hands (Q4 kickoff) run-of-show draft
- Opening (5 min): CEO framing — market posture and the thesis: serving > model ownership
- Exec snapshot (10 min): condensed highlights — OKR framing, cadence ask, hiring outlook
- Product demo (15 min): Dedicated beta milestones & Private onboarding playbook
- Reliability update (10 min): latency trends, outages prevented, FYI on streaming fallback
- Q&A + parking (15 min): live + Slack follow-up channel for questions
- Close & immediate asks (5 min): specific actions for teams before pre-kick (see immediate asks)

Exec update talking points (3–5 bullets)
- Market: increasing enterprise urgency for Dedicated SLAs — three active prospects requesting proof-of-privacy and capped latency guarantees.
- Ops: P95 has improved 14% over the last 6 weeks but still short of target; fallback streaming prototype reduces error amplification for longer prompts.
- Sales & Revenue: pipeline health strong but needs contractual guardrails for committed capacity to protect unit economics.
- People: temporarily restrict non-core hiring until finance confirms headcount uplift in Week 2.

Decision log (items we need exec sign-off on before pre-kick)
- Approve company OKR framing (yes/no)
- Approve 6-week cadence trial and define metrics for success at Week 7 (yes/no)
- Approve temporary hiring freeze and a narrow exceptions process (yes/no)

Risks & mitigations (top 5)
- Risk: Hiring freeze delays Dedicated capacity rollouts -> Mitigation: shift non-essential feature scope to Q1; use contractors for critical infra work.
- Risk: Cost degradation if caching/quantization pilots underperform -> Mitigation: set kill-switch criteria and run small-scale A/B tests with cost telemetry.
- Risk: Customer pilots fail due to onboarding gaps -> Mitigation: dedicate a Solutions eng buddy per pilot and freeze onboarding docs until pilot-ready checklist is passed.
- Risk: Cross-team mismatched priorities -> Mitigation: require a lead-level pre-kick alignment meeting and use the triage hour to rebalance weekly.
- Risk: Execs don’t align to cadence -> Mitigation: offer a 1-month extension option after the first 6-week trial and commit to presenting a results dashboard.

Immediate asks (owners + due dates)
- Product leads: finalize OKR language and link to Confluence page by 2026-03-15 (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Finance: confirm headcount policy and exceptions process by 2026-03-18 (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- SRE/Infra: baseline P95 reporting for top-10 routes and share dashboards by 2026-03-20 (owner: Jin Park)
- Solutions Eng: draft Dedicated + Private pilot support checklist by 2026-03-22 (owner: Evan Morales)

Follow-ups and next steps:
- Exec review session scheduled: 2026-03-23, 60 min (prep packet due 2026-03-20)
- All-hands draft slides circulated: 2026-03-25; rehearsal 2026-03-30
- Cadence pre-kick (OKR final sign-off): 2026-04-01

Notes / things to keep in mind:
- This doc intentionally leaves scope fuzzy for engineering deliverables to avoid blocking early sign-offs. Once OKRs are approved, teams should publish a one-pager per initiative with success metrics and risk heatmap.
- Communicate cadence change clearly in team-level standups the week after the exec decision; use the triage hour to smooth any friction.
